title: An MDF Claim the New Pre-Approval Rule No Longer Pays
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Tamarind Systems must decide whether a channel partner's market development funds (MDF) reimbursement claim can be paid, given how a comparable claim was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-03-12)**
Partner 'Aster Distribution' submitted an MDF reimbursement claim for $18,000 covering a co-marketing webinar it had already run, with no prior approval on file. Deal Desk APPROVED and reimbursed the claim. Note: 'Under the MDF rules then in effect, claims up to $25,000 could be reimbursed after the fact without documented pre-approval.'

**Current claim C (2024-10-21)**
Partner 'Basil Partners' submits a $16,500 MDF reimbursement claim for a regional trade-show booth it has already paid for and staffed. There is no pre-approval request on file. The partner wants the claim paid this quarter.

**MDF Claim Policy (current, effective 2024-06-01)**
All MDF-funded marketing activities must receive documented pre-approval from Deal Desk BEFORE the activity takes place. Claims submitted without a matching pre-approval are not reimbursable, regardless of dollar amount. The previous post-hoc reimbursement allowance for claims up to $25,000 was eliminated when this policy took effect.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
Partner AE: 'We paid Aster's claim back in March even though they never pre-registered the activity. Basil's claim is the same size and situation — let's just reimburse it too.'
Analyst: 'Aster was March, before the June MDF change. Let me confirm whether a post-hoc claim with no pre-approval is even payable anymore before I sign off.'

No pre-approval was ever filed for Basil's trade-show activity, and the claim was submitted only after the spend occurred.
question: How should the analyst handle Basil Partners' MDF reimbursement claim?
choices: Reimburse the claim to stay consistent with the March approval of Aster's comparable post-hoc MDF claim.
Deny the reimbursement: the March approval predates the June MDF policy change, and under the current rule a claim with no documented pre-approval is not payable regardless of amount.
Reimburse half of the claim as a compromise, since the trade-show activity genuinely occurred even though pre-approval was missing.
Escalate the claim to the VP of Channel for a one-time exception, treating the March payment as informal precedent.
